h.strategy: Use retrieved findings to classify settings as strong, weak, neutral or harmful, and to identify which settings can disconnect other parts from the outcome. Propose hypotheses only of two kinds. Self-conditioning: the edit's effect depends on the value it replaces, being more negative when that value is strong and more positive when it is empty or harmful. Disconnection: when the edited part cannot influence the outcome, its effect shrinks toward zero, so the direction is lower if the edit usually helps and higher if it usually hurts. Directions refer to the signed effect. For each hypothesis, state the edit's usual sign and a one-sentence mechanism. Cover varied edit fields and values. The critic should replace any hypothesis with an uncertain usual sign, competing effects or reliance on partial redundancy.

hyps.why: Edge 2 reaches the output only through edge 5, so with edge 5 removed the conv upgrade is disconnected and its usual gain vanishes.
Edge 1 feeds node 2, which reaches the output only via edge 5, so with edge 5 removed the conv upgrade has no path to the output.
Replacing an empty edge with a 3x3 conv adds a whole learnable path, whereas replacing an existing op gives a smaller gain.
Upgrading an already strong conv1x1 yields a marginal gain compared with upgrading a skip, pool or none edge.
Replacing a strong 3x3 conv with a parameter-free skip loses much more accuracy than replacing a weak op.
Removing a strong direct conv edge hurts more than removing a weak or already empty one, so the signed effect is more negative.
Pooling in place of an empty output edge adds a usable path, while pooling in place of a conv discards learned capacity.
A skip on an empty direct input-to-output edge adds a cheap gradient-friendly shortcut, a larger gain than replacing an op that already contributes.
Cutting the sole input edge into node 1 when it is a strong conv removes the main feature extractor for downstream edges, a bigger loss than removing a weak op.
Filling an empty direct input-to-output edge with a conv adds a short trainable path, a larger gain than replacing an op that already contributes.
